name: Templar
title: The heads of the biggest AI labs want to agree among themselves on when everyone should slow down. @TheEconomist's piece on that push ends with Covenant-72B, the model we finished training in March on GPUs contributed over the internet, as a reason such agreements may be hard to enforce. What the piece doesn't say is that once training no longer requires one giant, tightly connected cluster, the power to build new models no longer has to sit with a few companies. Globally distributed training and open models are essential tools for keeping that power from concentrating in the frontier labs. They let many more participants, from nations to companies, own a share of the future of AI and take part in building it. https://www.economist.com/international/2026/09/15/agreeing-to-make-ai-safer-may-be-impossible

name: Nige
title: RT by @nigescore: Astra Ultra did not cook sports-grade vision AI. Gave it a 30s football clip from our subnet private track. Frame-level events, JSON, annotated video. Ground truth and the published scoring rules only after it committed. 22 predictions. 17 real events. 15 inside the action windows. 7 extras. 2 misses. Precision 68.18%. Recall 88.24%. F1 76.92%. Our Bittensor eval, SN44: 0%. Matches after timing decay: 16.538 False positives: −20.300 GT weight: 25.600 score = max(0, (16.538 − 20.300) / 25.600) = 0 Three extra take-ons and two extra tackles were 14.6 penalty points. It also misread the late interception/clearance. Rare actions pay more when you hit them and tax you harder when you invent them. Perfect timestamps on the matches still would not have cleared that bill. This was one offline replay of the published scorer. Unchanged preds. Not live latency. Not a season. The point is simpler than the arithmetic. F1 is what you post. SN44 is what you get paid on. Real matches, messy cameras, hard negatives, and a 30-second clock are not the same sport as a nice 15s clip to aura farm on Twitter.

name: Templar
title: PULSE (also called Delta weight sync) has become one of the most important ideas in RL infrastructure this year. Our paper, posted on February 3, explained why it loses nothing. At RL learning rates, about 99% of each step's weight updates disappear in the BF16 cast, so the inference workers never see them. Since then, @huggingface has built Delta Weight Sync for TRL and vLLM on that argument. @FireworksAI_HQ cites PULSE, and its ARCv3 compressor now makes the updates even smaller. This week @humansand reported pausing inference for only about 220 milliseconds per update on Blackwell GPUs. PULSE has now been accepted at AXIOM, a @NeurIPSConf 2026 workshop. https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.03839

name: Jacob Steeves
title: Yesterday we released rolling hash wallets (like Bitcoin) and Quantum protected wallets. They combine together: you can wrap a quantum wallet under rolling hashes, multi-sig it, and use a vault signer, with a transaction delay. You'd need to crack both Sha256 and quantum encryption -- at the same time -- to touch them.
